raw_findings.text: The HARE_MD_HEAD constant hardcodes '- (none yet)' for the owner's rules section, but apply_rules only preserves content outside the marked block. If an owner adds hand-written rules, they live above the block and survive; the placeholder text is only used when the file is empty or missing the markers. Placeholder text in HARE_MD_HEAD only shows on fresh files; owner lines above the block are preserved. No change needed; the design intentionally separates owner rules (above) from ledger rules (inside the block).

proposed_rules is called twice when the file changes: once for the print line and once inside apply_rules. Cheap but wasteful. proposed_rules(ledger) runs twice on write path. Store the result in a variable and reuse it for both the print and the apply_rules call.

The base_ref used to fetch HARE.md falls back to 'main' when base.sha is missing. On a PR from a fork, base.sha exists but the file may not exist on that ref; the try/except swallows the 404 and returns empty string, which is fine. However, if the base branch is not 'main' (e.g., a release branch), the fallback to 'main' could fetch the wrong HARE.md. The PR's base ref should be used consistently. Fallback to 'main' for HARE.md fetch may read wrong branch when base is not main. Use base_ref from the PR's base.sha without a 'main' fallback; if the file is missing on that ref, let the exception return empty string.

The PR body template in the workflow still says 'wrote | scripts/hare_ledger.py (no model) | low | AI wrote it' but the script now also writes HARE.md. The Models table should reflect that the ledger job updates two artifacts. Workflow PR body Models table doesn't mention HARE.md output. Update the PR body template to note HARE.md is also written by the ledger run.

The rules block header text is duplicated between rules_block() and HARE_MD_HEAD. If the header wording changes, it must be updated in two places. Duplicated header text in rules_block and HARE_MD_HEAD. Extract the header into a constant or helper so there's a single source of truth.

proposed_rules() is called twice in main() — once for the write and once for the print — which re-sorts and re-deduplicates unnecessarily. proposed_rules called twice in main; compute once and reuse. Store the result in a variable and reuse it for both the write and the log line.

HARE.md is fetched from the base branch but truncated to 8000 chars without any indication. A large HARE.md could lose the rules block entirely. HARE.md silently truncated to 8000 chars; rules block could be cut. Either raise the cap, truncate only the owner's section, or add a note when truncation happens.

This conflates budget exhaustion with other empty-answer causes in the 'not the token budget' headline.
